summary: Episode 4 of the Ramadan Daily Tafsir series focuses on Surah Ar-Ra'd (Chapter 13), a Meccan chapter that centers on the theme of Tawhid (monotheism) that Prophet Muhammad brought to the Arabs. The lecture explains the meaning of the abbreviated letters (Alif-Lam-Meem-Ra) at the beginning of the chapter and discusses the distinction between Meccan and Medinan surahs—a distinction based on time period rather than geographical location. The speaker emphasizes that the Qur'an's arguments about Allah raising the heavens without pillars are not meant to prove Allah's existence (which the Arabs already acknowledged) but rather to affirm that Allah alone deserves worship without partners.
